decisions.decision: v1 prompts 11, 12 and 13 are absorbed into S32, S33/S34 and S36, where their text stays normative.
decisions.rationale: They were never started, and v2 rebuilds the foundations they depend on (shared stage, Formula Core, Figure Kit, tokens).

decisions.decision: The v2 pack is strictly sequential: one prompt at a time, each requiring its predecessor to be done.
decisions.rationale: Requested by the maintainer so a single agent can execute each prompt completely without coordination.

decisions.decision: Recorded that CI-equivalent runs use the classic WebGLRenderer, not the node renderer's WebGL2 backend.
decisions.rationale: With --disable-blink-features=WebGPU, navigator.gpu exists but requestAdapter() is null; createRenderer throws and retries classic WebGLRenderer (programs read from info.programs; node renderers use info.memory.programs). The S01 context text and render-architecture assumptions for CI should be corrected.

decisions.decision: Added an 0xRRGGBB column to the colour-literal audit and kept per-view gpuFrameMs null where no WebGPU timestamp device exists.
decisions.rationale: F-04 quotes ~199 hex literals but grep finds 83 #hex and 230 0xRRGGBB; the column makes the discrepancy re-runnable. Per-view GPU time needs trackTimestamp at renderer construction (S04), so the harness uses a throw-away reference-scene probe, unvalidated here because WebGPU is unusable in the sandbox (Chromium 141 + SwiftShader).

decisions.decision: S01 branch was fast-forwarded onto origin/claude/eloquent-bardeen-8rt6ch, which carries the ledger and prompt pack that are not on main.
decisions.rationale: Step 1 requires the ledger; main did not contain it. The two docs-only commits ride in the S01 PR.

decisions.decision: cividis is documented as Battelle-licensed, not CC0.
decisions.rationale: The prompt calls viridis, magma and cividis CC0. The primary source (pnnl/cmaputil LICENSE, Battelle Memorial Institute) is a BSD-style licence; only mpl-colormaps (viridis, magma) is CC0. The notice is reproduced in js/design/palette-data.mjs.

decisions.decision: Machado 2009 matrices (11 severities per type) transcribed from colour-science machado2010.py (BSD-3-Clause).
decisions.rationale: The authors' page (inf.ufrgs.br) was blocked by the sandbox proxy. Severity-1.0 matrices match the published values; intermediate severities interpolate between the 0.1-step tables.

decisions.decision: Status tokens adjusted to pass ΔE00 >= 12 for normal, protan, deutan and tritan vision. Before -> after (OKLCH): established 0.78 0.10 160 -> 0.814 0.085 141.7; effective 0.78 0.10 200 -> 0.78 0.098 197.6; schematic 0.80 0.10 85 -> 0.806 0.13 89.6; conjectural 0.72 0.12 295 -> unchanged; open 0.70 0.13 25 -> 0.668 0.13 23; heuristic 0.80 0.10 85 -> 0.661 0.136 100.4.
decisions.rationale: schematic and heuristic were identical (ΔE00 0), so every pair failed. Minimal-displacement search, all six >= 4.5:1 text contrast on every surface. Existing .badge-* CSS keeps its own colours so the atlas looks the same; badges adopt --status-* later.

decisions.decision: Canvas labels below 10 px (8, 9, 9.5 px in mod-qft, mod-experiments, mod-planck, extras) keep their exact size via tokens.font.monoPx(px) instead of snapping to a type step. extras.jsx used 'var(--font-mono)' inside canvas font strings, which canvas ignores; they now resolve to the real mono family.
decisions.rationale: Moving to step -2 (10.42 px) or the 10 px floor would change pixels, against 'the atlas must look the same'. The Figure Kit (S09) replaces these labels. The extras.jsx change is the only intended pixel difference and is not captured by a baseline.

decisions.decision: ~220 frozen --pigment-* tokens preserve the exact legacy scene colours; tweaks-panel.jsx (self-contained light-theme widget at the repo root) is out of scope; float-triple three.js colours became color(srgb-linear …) tokens; bh-mobile-lab fails on the untouched base too (49,630 px).
decisions.rationale: Naming one-off shades semantically per scene is S-later work and would risk visible drift. The lint covers all of js/ (wider than the prompt's paths). The bh-mobile-lab baseline was not refreshed.

decisions.decision: compileTSL returns { node, terms } instead of a bare node carrying terms. The GPU spec uses compileTSL(...).node where the prompt writes vec4(compileTSL(...), ...).
decisions.rationale: Attaching terms to the returned node would mutate shared TSL nodes (a lone symbol returns the caller's own binding). A wrapper object is safe and the prompt requires terms to be returned.

decisions.decision: Reference DOIs and arXiv ids in js/formula/library were NOT machine-verified and carry no retrieval date: crossref.org, arxiv.org and doi.org are blocked by the build environment proxy (403). Numeric values were verified by computation instead (see evidence.measurements). M_sun stays at the repo/prompt value 1.98847e30 kg; IAU 2015 nominal GM_sun / CODATA 2018 G gives 1.98841e30 (3e-5 relative), kept so the library equals js/physics.mjs to 1e-12.
decisions.rationale: Same situation as D-007. The citations are the standard primary sources for each formula, written from knowledge; a follow-up with network access should confirm them and add retrieval dates.

decisions.decision: Library formulas are defined once in SI with physical constants as symbols carrying their SI value; "geometric units" means binding every constant to 1 (formula.geometric). gpuSafe and the GPU spec sample geometric units by default. Mathematical pi is the literal PI node, not a symbol.
decisions.rationale: Single definition for SI wrappers and GPU use. SI evaluation of e.g. planckLength underflows float32, so GPU safety is only meaningful in geometric units; a test pins that.

decisions.decision: to-tsl maps integer powers |n| <= 8 to multiplication chains, p/q = 1/2 to sqrt and 1/3 to cbrt (tsl.cbrt, not in the prompt list), other powers to tsl.pow. lt/gt used as values compile to select(cmp, 1, 0); select requires an lt/gt condition. The webgpu spec case is annotated and skipped when no adapter exists, so the webgl2 case is the CI gate. Float render targets were readable on SwiftShader, so the HalfFloat fallback was not needed. Locally the installed Playwright wants chromium 1208 but 1194 is installed; the run used executablePath with a throw-away config (not committed).
decisions.rationale: pow() of a negative base is undefined in GLSL/WGSL and x*x matches the JS evaluator; cbrt is exported by three.tsl.js r186; the rest keeps the semantics of the JS evaluator.
